Isobel is a half-elf and cleric of  Selûne, who is protecting Last Light Inn in the Shadow-Cursed Lands during Act Two. She can also become a Camp Follower.
“
"Tell me, do you believe in love at first sight?
„
— Isobel, speaking of Dame Aylin

Overview

Isobel is a cleric of Selûne who is helping a group of Harpers stationed at the Last Light Inn. She has been using her Selûnite magic to maintain the moon shield that is protecting the inn from the Shadow Curse. Without her protection, the inhabitants of the inn would succumb to the Shadow Curse.

History

Isobel is the daughter of  Ketheric Thorm and  Melodia Thorm, raised in her mother's footsteps as a follower of  Selûne. After Melodia's passing, Ketheric raised Isobel alone, staying true to their Selûnite ways despite his doubts.

Over one hundred years ago,  Dame Aylin, daughter of the Moonmaiden, was sent as an emissary of Selûne to Isobel's town, where the two fell in love at first sight. Ketheric was opposed to their relationship. Isobel believed it was because Aylin was immortal, which caused an 'imbalance' in their relationship. Aylin herself thought that Ketheric did not trust her and was threatened by their love. For Isobel, however, there was no question of their being together: "loving Aylin felt the same as loving myself."

Some time later, Isobel died in an unknown manner.[2] Grief-stricken, Ketheric turned to  Shar and tricked Aylin, luring her into the Shadowfell, where she was captured and imprisoned, her life force suborned to grant him immortality. Later, he entered into a dark bargain with and became the chosen of  Myrkul, in return for being able to fully restore Isobel to life.[3]

Newly alive, disoriented and with a deep feeling of filth within herself, Isobel saw a change in her father.[4] With his strange demeanour and declaration that Aylin was dead, Isobel could see no recourse but to run. She found the Last Light Inn, where she created a shelter from the surrounding Shadow-Curse. By the time Jaheira and her Harpers arrived, Isobel had pieced together that she had been dead a hundred years and that Ketheric was responsible for the horrors plaguing the land. She can be seen muttering "why did you change" to the elven bust of her father inside her room.

Involvement

Act Two

Isobel is on the top floor of the Last Light Inn in the Shadow-Cursed Lands.  Jaheira directs the party toward her to receive  Blessing of Selûne for moderate protection against the Shadow Curse, gaining the ⁠Shield of the Moon inspiration for party members with the  Soldier background. Isobel blesses the party even if they have other means of protection.

Attempting kidnapping

Speaking to her at Last Light Inn instigates a conversation with Flaming Fist  Marcus, who summons several winged ghouls in an attempt to kidnap Isobel and take her to Moonrise Towers. This starts ⁠Resolve the Abduction. If the party choose to side with Isobel, and Marcus and the ghouls are defeated, then she continues to sustain her warding over Last Light Inn. If she is instead defeated in combat, she is immediately abducted, the fight ends and the warding fails. Then the party must fight against the remaining Harpers outside, as well as some Vines, although Jaheira remains as an uncontrolled ally.

If the party choose to side with Marcus, they must fight Isobel and the Harpers inside the Inn, including Jaheira.[5] Once Isobel is defeated, the warding over Last Light's Inn falters, and the party must fight against the remaining Harpers outside, as well as some Vines.

If Isobel remains after the fight with Marcus, the  Dark Urge finds themselves desiring to kill her.  Sceleritas Fel also appears at camp to task the Urge with her death. Isobel helps to talk the Urge down, explaining that as an experienced cleric she can see when the Urge is and is not being themselves. The Urge can return and break their truce at any time.

If at any point the Dark Urge fails to suppress their urges, the moon shield falls with Isobel dead, causing all within (save Jaheira) to fall to the curse. Killing Isobel also grants the inspiration ⁠Lunar Eclipse.

Assault on Moonrise Towers

If the  Nightsong is killed, Isobel becomes overwhelmed and unable to sustain her protection over the Inn, killing her and all others within.

Otherwise, if the Nightsong is released, she moves to the inn's courtyard where she urges the party to go to Moonrise Towers. After Ketheric is defeated, Isobel travels to Moonrise Towers where she reunites with her lover,  Dame Aylin. She asks the party if the two of them may remain at camp for a time, to answer some questions for  Shadowheart.

If Isobel is captured by Marcus, she aids  Ketheric Thorm in the fight inside the illithid colony. She cannot be saved here and dies at the end of the fight even if she manages to stay alive until its end.

Attacking Isobel in the Shadow-Cursed Lands after Ketheric has retreated turns Jaheira against the party.

If they both remain alive, Isobel and Aylin become Camp Followers and travel with the party to Baldur's Gate.

Act Three

Isobel remains with the party at their Campsite together with Dame Aylin, if they were invited to stay at the end of Act Two. They both remain there until  Lorroakan is defeated, upon which they leave to help a Selûnite enclave outside the city. The two later appear at the High Hall during the final fight to ⁠lend aid.

If Aylin is allowed to be caged by Lorroakan, the party can convince Isobel that he overpowered both of them. Isobel then leaves for Ramazith's Tower to save Aylin, but is defeated and can later be found dead in the tower. A heartbroken Aylin vows that once she escapes, she will kill the party's "children, and their children beside".

Datamined content

Some datamined content reveals her original backstory. She was supposed to have been killed by  Balthazar, and Aylin was framed for her murder. Ketheric turned Aylin into the Nightsong as an act of revenge. A century later, Ketheric tasked Balthazar with bringing Isobel back. This ritual also bound Isobel's life to Ketheric, sharing his immortality with her. If Ketheric was killed before untethering Isobel from him, they would both go to the afterlife. See Aylin/Cut_content for more.

Notes and References

  1. ↑ Isobel's kinship with Thisobald is unclear. Though Thisobald refers to Ketheric as "Father" and introduces himself as "Son of Thorm", neither Ketheric nor Isobel ever acknowledges him in dialogue or otherwise. Given that Ketheric and Balthazar have desecrated the Thorm mausoleum and resurrected Isobel, it is possible that Thisobald is another resurrected relative and refers to Ketheric as father, not in the paternal sense, but as "creator". Also noteworthy is that in  The Waning Moon: Consignments, Thisobald calls him "Father Ketheric", which makes it more likely that Thisobald is referring to Ketheric as a principal figure of Shar rather than a literal parent, similar to how Shadowheart refers to Viconia DeVir as "Mother".
  2. ↑ If the party talk to  Squire using  Speak with Animals, she can reveal that she died the same night as Isobel while trying to protect her, hinting that Isobel might have been murdered.
  3. ↑ Although Ketheric's other family members –  Thisobald,  Malus, and  Gerringothe – are Undead monsters, Isobel is not. As the party progress through Act Two, it is revealed that Ketheric was utterly devastated by her loss and was ultimately willing to go to extraordinary lengths and pay any price to have her returned to him.
  4. ↑  Isobel's Diary
  5. ↑ Any enemies killed during this initial fight do not seem to grant experience, even if a player character lands the killing blow; this may be a bug.
